proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 3, proof of Theorem 1.6 "⇒" (chapter-03.txt lines 113–143), which compares blow-ups of M and of its pieces using the Upper Density Theorem, Ch. 1, 3.6 and Remark 3.7(2) (chapter-01.txt lines 700–725). The Upper Density Theorem is formalized in SimonGMT as Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.simon_theorem_3_6 and ae_dimensionalUpperDensity_eq_zero_outside_of_openSigmaFinite (Chapter01/DensityComparison.lean). Notation: Hⁿ = μHE[n]; η_{x,λ}(z) = λ⁻¹(z − x); B_s(x) is the open ball.
1. Put D := B ∖ A, a Borel subset of U. For every compact K ⊆ U, Hⁿ(D ∩ K) ≤ Hⁿ(B ∩ K) < ∞. Write U = ⋃_m V_m with V_m := {x ∈ U : |x| < m, dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ U) > 1/m} (open, with compact closure in U; V_m := {|x| < m} if U = ℝ^P). Then Hⁿ(D ∩ V_m) < ∞.
2. Apply the Upper Density Theorem (Ch. 1, 3.6) to the Borel regular measure Hⁿ and the Hⁿ-measurable set D ∩ V_m of finite measure. For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∉ D ∩ V_m we get limsup_{s↓0} s^{−n} Hⁿ(D ∩ V_m ∩ B_s(x)) = 0. Let E_m be the exceptional Hⁿ-null set and E := ⋃_m E_m, again Hⁿ-null. Mathlib's μHE[n] is a positive constant multiple of the Hausdorff measure normalization used by SimonGMT, so null sets and vanishing upper densities are the same for both.
3. Let x ∈ A ∖ E. Then x ∉ D (as A ∩ D = ∅) and x ∈ V_m for some m. Since V_m is an open neighbourhood of x, D ∩ V_m ∩ B_s(x) = D ∩ B_s(x) for small s > 0. Hence
 (∗) s^{−n} Hⁿ(D ∩ B_s(x)) → 0 as s ↓ 0.
4. Fix such an x and f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with spt f ⊆ B_R(0), R > 0. Choose λ₀ > 0 with B̄_{λ₀R}(x) ⊆ U, and let 0 < λ < λ₀ and η := η_{x,λ}.
 (a) η is a homeomorphism of ℝ^P, so η(B) is the disjoint union of the Borel sets η(A) and η(D).
 (b) Hⁿ is translation invariant and Hⁿ(λ⁻¹S) = λ^{−n}Hⁿ(S) (Mathlib Measure.hausdorffMeasure_smul₀). So η(B) ∩ B_R(0) = η(B ∩ B_{λR}(x)) has measure λ^{−n}Hⁿ(B ∩ B_{λR}(x)) < ∞.
 (c) Hence f is integrable on η(B), η(A) and η(D), and ∫_{η(B)} f dHⁿ − ∫_{η(A)} f dHⁿ = ∫_{η(D)} f dHⁿ.
5. By (b): |∫_{η(D)} f dHⁿ| ≤ sup|f| · Hⁿ(η(D) ∩ B_R(0)) = sup|f| · λ^{−n} Hⁿ(D ∩ B_{λR}(x)) = sup|f| · Rⁿ · (λR)^{−n} Hⁿ(D ∩ B_{λR}(x)). By (∗) this tends to 0 as λ ↓ 0. For n = 0 the same computation holds with Rⁿ = 1.
6. Therefore ∫_{η_{x,λ}(B)} f dHⁿ − ∫_{η_{x,λ}(A)} f dHⁿ → 0 as λ ↓ 0, for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P). Consequently, for every linear subspace Q of ℝ^P, the blow-up integrals of B converge to ∫_Q f dHⁿ for all f if and only if those of A do. The condition dim Q = n is common to both sides. Hence HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q ⟺ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q for every Q.
7. Step 6 holds for every x ∈ A ∖ E, and Hⁿ(E) = 0. So it holds for (Hⁿ⌞A)-a.e. x, which is the assertion. ∎
key_steps: D := B ∖ A has locally finite Hⁿ-measure in U; by the Upper Density Theorem (Ch. 1, 3.6/3.7(2)), s^{−n}Hⁿ(D ∩ B_s(x)) → 0 for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ A.
For such x, blow-up integrals over η_{x,λ}(B) and η_{x,λ}(A) differ by ∫_{η_{x,λ}(D)} f, bounded by sup|f| Rⁿ (λR)^{−n} Hⁿ(D ∩ B_{λR}(x)) → 0.
Hence both sets have the same approximate tangent spaces at every such x.
